about.title: How Chatter is built
about.lead: Chatter is a small, independent chat. This page shows what it runs on, where your data goes and how long it stays there, so that you can judge it for yourself.
about.partsIntro: What runs where, and what each part is for.

website.name: The website
website.text: The page you are looking at: a static app built with React. It is served from Cloudflare's network and holds no data of its own.

chat.name: The chat server
chat.text: Carries every message in real time over an encrypted connection. It checks names, limits and bans before anything is passed on.

redis.name: Redis
redis.text: Keeps what is short-lived: the last messages of each room, the latest announcement and the proof that lets you come back as yourself after a dropped connection.

admin.name: The admin
admin.text: Where moderators manage rooms, bans and reports, and where the terms and the privacy policy are written.

postgres.name: The database
postgres.text: Holds what has to last: accounts, rooms, bans, reports and the texts of the terms and the privacy policy.

server.name: The server
server.text: One small machine in Germany runs the chat server, the admin, the database and Redis in Docker. Caddy takes care of HTTPS and its certificates.

backups.name: Backups
backups.text: The database is copied every night, and the copies are kept for 30 days.

monitoring.name: Monitoring
monitoring.text: Checks every few minutes that the website, the chat server and the admin answer. It sees no messages.

journey.write: You write a message. Your browser sends it over an encrypted WebSocket connection (TLS) to the chat server.
journey.check: The server checks the room, the length, the slow mode, the rate limits and whether you are banned.
journey.keep: The message is kept in Redis as one of the room's last 50, and is deleted an hour after the room's last message.
journey.deliver: It is sent to everyone in the room at once.

about.journeyPrivate: A private message skips the storing: it goes only to the two people in it, and the server does not keep it. Your browser keeps the open conversations in this tab, so that a reload does not lose them.
about.dataTitle: What is kept, and for how long
about.dataIntro: Only what the chat needs to work, and for as short a time as possible.

messages.what: Messages in a room, and their reactions
messages.where: Redis, the last 50 messages of each room
messages.howLong: Deleted an hour after the room's last message

private.where: Not on the server; only in the open tabs of the two people

guest.what: A guest's nickname, avatar and age
guest.where: In the server's memory while you are connected, and in this tab of your browser
guest.howLong: The server forgets them when the connection ends; the tab, when it is closed

account.what: An account: the sign-in provider and your id there, email, username, display name, picture, gender and age
account.howLong: Until you delete the account in your profile

address.where: Used while you are connected, to limit abuse; otherwise kept only as a salted hash (with messages and reports), so that a ban can find them
address.howLong: The hash goes with the message, so an hour; with a report, 90 days

reports.what: A reported message, its sender's hash and the reasons

safety.limits: Slow mode, rate limits and a cap per address stop floods and spam.
safety.reports: Anyone can report a message. When three different addresses have reported it, it is hidden for everybody until a moderator has looked at it.
safety.bans: Bans work on a salted hash of the address, so the address itself is not kept. Moderators are people with an account in the admin.
safety.age: You must be 18 or older. There is no way to check an age, so this rests on the terms and on moderation.
safety.passwords: Accounts have no password: you sign in with Google, Facebook or Discord, and Chatter receives your name and email, never your password. Moderators' passwords are stored hashed.
safety.thirdParties: The site has no advertising and no tracking scripts. Your browser talks to the site, to the chat server and, when you search for GIFs, to GIPHY. Avatars are drawn in your browser.
safety.headers: The site sends strict security headers: its Content-Security-Policy only lets it run its own scripts and load GIFs from GIPHY.

about.build: The code is open: anybody can read it. Every change is checked automatically before it goes live: formatting, types, hundreds of unit tests and browser tests that run the real chat server. Only a change that passes is built into images and put on the server by GitHub Actions.

limits.hobby: Chatter is run by one person on one small server. It is built to be reliable, but it is not a company: it can be down for a while, and no uptime is promised.
limits.public: What you write in a room is seen by everybody in it, and moderators can read it. Do not share anything you would not say in public.
limits.law: The terms of use and the privacy policy are the binding texts; this page explains the same things in plain words.

info.title: How the chat works
info.everyone: What you write goes to everybody in the room, unless you have chosen a person next to the message box.
info.private: Choose a person next to the message box, or click one of their messages, to write only to them. Private messages only reach people who are in the same room right now, and are kept only in this tab.
info.conversations: Private conversations are listed under Direct messages, next to the message box. A number shows how many messages you have not read; opening the conversation clears it. The bell next to a person stops notifications from them, and the switch above the list stops them from everybody.
info.blocking: Open a private conversation to block somebody who bothers you. Their messages then no longer reach you, you can't write to them, and they are told that you blocked them. You can unblock them at any time.
info.keyboard: Tab goes to the messages you can act on. Then use the up and down arrows to move between them, Home and End to jump to the oldest and newest, and Enter to write to the person whose message it is. R opens the reactions for the message. Tab again leaves the messages.
info.moderators: People with a green Moderator badge look after the chat. They can post announcements to the whole room.
